summary: FilmCraft is a video editor, like Adobe Premiere Pro. You put clips, pictures, music, titles and subtitles on a timeline. Then you export 1 video.
use_cases: Edit a 30-second social media video from pictures, a short animation and music.
Add a name title and subtitles to an interview. Export an MP4 video and a subtitle file.
Make a slideshow with soft fades for a birthday or a team event.
When a picture or a number changes, make the same video again from the saved list of steps.
story: FilmCraft edited the 20-second video that connects the apps. It starts with the PhotoCraft header picture. Then it shows the EffectCraft card, the GridCraft table and a sound-wave picture of the SoundCraft tune. A Python script drew that picture. Soft fades connect the parts. The SoundCraft tune is the music. A label says "Illustrative synthetic data" during the full video. Subtitles tell you that every number is a share of the conversation.
recipe: filmcraft-cli --project teaser.fcproj exec file.exportMedia path=teaser.mp4 burnCaptions=true wait=true
recipe_note: Build the video edit from a list of steps. Export the video with subtitles. Then save 1 frame as a picture.

assets.caption: The 20-second video has music and subtitles. It uses media from PhotoCraft, EffectCraft, GridCraft and SoundCraft. The data is invented.
assets.description: A list of steps told FilmCraft where to put each clip, fade, label and subtitle. FilmCraft then made the video and its sound in 1 export.
assets.how: filmcraft-cli --compact run build_all.jsonl --save-as signal_noise_teaser.fcproj; filmcraft-cli --project signal_noise_teaser.fcproj exec file.exportMedia '{"path":"signal_noise_teaser.mp4","format":"h264","bitrateKbps":1400,"bitrateMode":"vbr1Pass","hardwareEncoding":"off","burnCaptions":true,"captionSidecar":"vtt","wait":true}' (1280x720, 30 fps, H.264 + AAC)

assets.caption: Frame at 2 seconds: the PhotoCraft header with a FilmCraft subtitle and label.
assets.description: FilmCraft drew this frame from the saved edit. The page uses it as the preview image of the video.

assets.caption: The silent GIF preview of the video is 576 × 324 pixels.
assets.description: FilmCraft exported the same edit as a small GIF without sound. Use it where a video does not play.

assets.caption: The frame at 10 s shows the EffectCraft card with the FilmCraft label.
assets.description: FilmCraft drew the frame at 10 seconds.

assets.caption: Frame at 16.5 s: a FilmCraft fade blends the GridCraft table into the sound-wave picture. A subtitle shows below.
assets.description: FilmCraft drew this frame in the middle of a cross-dissolve. The two pictures blend at half strength. The subtitle stays readable above the label.
assets.how: filmcraft-cli --project signal_noise_teaser.fcproj render --seconds 16.5 --out signal_noise_teaser_frame_mix.png (mid-point of the 0.5 s cross_dissolve, 16.233-16.733 s)

assets.caption: The subtitle file (WebVTT) holds the text of the video subtitles.
assets.description: FilmCraft wrote the subtitles into this separate file during the video export.

assets.caption: The FilmCraft project of the video holds the timeline, fades, label, subtitles and markers.
assets.description: FilmCraft saved the project after it did the list of steps. The download does not include the media files.
assets.how: Saved by filmcraft-cli run build_all.jsonl --save-as signal_noise_teaser.fcproj

assets.caption: This list holds the steps that build the video edit, 1 step per line.
assets.description: Small Python programs wrote this list. FilmCraft did the steps and built the full edit.
assets.how: Python writes JSONL lines (file.newSequence, file.import, file.newColorMatte, timeline.place, effects.setParam, sequence.applyVideoTransition, graphics.newText/newShape/set, captions.newTrack/setStyle/add, markers.add); filmcraft-cli run executes them.

headless_notes: All work used filmcraft-cli run, exec, render and probe. No window opened and no sound played. The PhotoCraft header and the GridCraft table are their v2 files; the edit waited for both .v2-ready markers. Clip and item numbers are in creation order, so the command list uses fixed numbers. A test import of the exported MP4 showed the burned-in subtitles. probe showed H.264 High, 1280x720, 30 fps, with AAC sound. Python measured the exported sound: peak -1.0 dBFS, RMS -18.3 dBFS. GIF frame times round to 120 ms, so the GIF plays about 4% fast. Subtitles sit at the bottom center, above the label: captions.setStyle {anchor: bottom, margin: 0.15}. The WebVTT file stores no position, so video players use their default bottom position.
